fields.title: Software Engineer
fields.bio:
Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication in distributed systems.
I am Qefser Karpuzi. My engineering thesis is simple: complex problems do not require complex, brittle code. I focus on developing clean, highly testable backend systems and responsive web platforms that execute perfectly under heavy operational loads.

Operating as an instructor at Scantech Academy demands absolute mastery over the core rules of computing. When you are tasked with deconstructing complex data flow, network pipelines, and memory allocation for advanced cohorts, you cannot afford to rely on surface-level framework abstractions. That foundational discipline dictates every line of code I write.

Whether scaling database query engines, designing resilient APIs, or rendering fast client interfaces, my focus remains squarely on system reliability, minimal operational overhead, and long-term business viability.

fields.title: Eli Propreté — Business Website
fields.short_description: Full-stack website for a cleaning services business, built with PHP and MySQL, deployed on Hostinger.
fields.description:
Designed and built the complete website for Eli Propreté, a cleaning services business based in France — from database schema to frontend.

Built with PHP and MySQL, developed locally on XAMPP with phpMyAdmin, and deployed to production on Hostinger. Includes a services catalog, project gallery, and a working contact form for quote requests.

Owned the project end-to-end: layout and visual design, backend logic, database structure, and hosting/deployment.

fields.title: AAB College AI Assistant
fields.short_description: Domain-specific AI chatbot for AAB College, built on a self-hosted LLM and a custom hybrid retrieval system.
fields.description:
Built an AI-powered assistant that answers student and staff questions in Albanian, using content scraped from the college's own site, a curated FAQ database, and structured lookups for locations and staff.

Runs entirely on self-hosted infrastructure — no third-party AI API. Uses a quantized local LLM via Ollama solely to rewrite retrieved content into natural Albanian, not to generate answers from its own knowledge, keeping every response grounded in real source data.

Built a hybrid retrieval engine from scratch combining semantic search (sentence-transformer embeddings), BM25 keyword scoring, and a custom entity-disambiguation layer for handling ambiguous name/topic queries — plus a hand-written typo-correction and stemming pipeline for Albanian, a language with minimal existing NLP tooling.

Currently in active development in collaboration with a team; not yet deployed to production.

fields.title: AI Document Classification System
fields.short_description: AI-powered system that extracts and classifies documents across PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and image formats — built as a Bachelor's thesis project.
fields.description:
Bachelor's thesis: a Django-based system that automates document archiving by extracting text and classifying content across mixed formats — PDF, scanned images, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint — into one of fourteen predefined categories, with no manual tagging required.

For scanned or image-based documents, text is extracted via Tesseract OCR (through pytesseract) with PDF pages rendered through pdf2image/Poppler first. Digitally-authored files are parsed directly from their native structure using python-docx, openpyxl, and python-pptx. Classification runs on a hand-tuned, weighted keyword-scoring algorithm with word-boundary matching for precision.

To validate the approach, I ran a comparative experiment against traditional Machine Learning — training Naive Bayes and SVM models (scikit-learn) on a labeled 85-document dataset — to evaluate whether a trained model would outperform the keyword-based system, and at what cost. Findings and tradeoffs are documented in full in the thesis writeup.

Includes role-based access control (Administrator vs. regular user), a searchable document archive, and category management. Verified through unit testing, which surfaced and led to fixing a real keyword-matching bug during development.
